mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for 3 consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 5% for 3 consecutive months signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for 2 consecutive months reduces labor market demand, lowering equity risk premia and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in rising unemployment periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for 2 consecutive months signals labor market strength that compresses discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in recovery periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production above 112.0 for 3 consecutive months indicates expanding domestic demand, lowering discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in expanding demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in consumer price inflation above 2.0% for 3 consecutive months signals supply-side pressures that compress discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rising inflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decrease in the S&P 500 index below 1400 for 3 consecutive months indicates weak investor demand, lowering discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in weak demand periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decrease in industrial production below 112.0 for 3 consecutive months indicates contracting domestic demand, compressing discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in contracting demand periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
